name: ICICI Life Insurance Ltd
title: ICICI Life Insurance Ltd - 540133 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Life insurer H1 VNB up 22.3% to ₹12.83bn with margin 26.0% driven by protection mix, but management flagged a consultation paper threatening credit-life and renewal-commission economics and gave no growth guidance.

triggers.label: IRDAI consultation paper on commissions
triggers.quote: IRDAI has released a public consultation paper on recalibrating economics of insurance distribution.

triggers.label: Retail protection growth to taper in H2
triggers.quote: those growth numbers should taper down from the 40%-50% that we've been seeing to more moderate levels

triggers.label: Linked savings APE growth 6.6%
triggers.quote: Linked business grew by 6.6% year-on-year in H1-FY2027.

triggers.label: VNB up 22.3%, margin 26.0%
triggers.quote: VNB growing by 22.3% to ₹ 12.83 billion in H1 -FY2027, and margins stood at 26.0%.

red_flags.label: Credit-life commission cap under consultation
red_flags.quote: It does propose a fairly significant cut

red_flags.label: Persistency softening
red_flags.quote: 25th month persistency is like 76.2%, which is fallen from June, 77%

red_flags.label: Management declines guidance and key details

evasions.quote: It's a little too early to call.
we've not broken the entire walk at this point

summary.headline: H1-FY27 VNB rose 22.3% to ₹12.83 billion, with VNB margin at 26.0% on a protection-led mix shift.
summary.overview: ICICI Life reported H1-FY27 VNB up 22.3% YoY to ₹12.83 billion, with margin at 26.0% versus 24.7% for FY26, attributed mainly to product mix toward protection. Total premium grew 15.3% to ₹245.05 billion and new business premium 25.0% to ₹118.21 billion, while protection APE rose 39.5%. Linked savings slowed to 6.6% growth amid equity market softness, and non-linked savings fell 4.5% for H1 though Q2 recovered to near last year's level. Management was cautious on IRDAI's distribution consultation paper (credit life and commission caps), declining to quantify its impact, and gave no formal guidance.

segments.name: Protection
segments.commentary: Protection APE grew 39.5% YoY; protection share of APE rose to 23.4% from 19.3%. Sum assured grew 30.1% to ₹8.81 trillion, with 11.5% sum assured market share; retail protection sum assured up 47.2%.

segments.name: Savings (APE ₹37.79 billion)
segments.commentary: Savings APE up 9.3% YoY, with annuity up about 50%. Linked grew 6.6% and softened in late Q2; non-linked fell 4.5% for H1 but Q2 was near last year's level. Group funds grew 48%.

segments.name: Agency
segments.commentary: H1 premium ₹11.02 billion, up 3.3% YoY; Q2 growth 4.1%. Gross agent additions up 23%.

segments.name: Direct
segments.commentary: H1 premium ₹6.79 billion, up 10.9% YoY; NRI push via GIFT City.

segments.name: Bancassurance
segments.commentary: Grew 4.6% YoY, 27.4% of APE. ICICI Bank is about half of banca and broadly steady at ₹100-120 crore per month.

segments.name: Partnership distribution
segments.commentary: Grew 34.1% YoY, 14.8% of APE; 1,600+ partners, none other than ICICI Bank above 5% of APE.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance given; management said it provides medium-term direction only.
Retail protection growth (40-50% in recent quarters) expected to taper to more moderate levels in H2 FY27.
Margin framed as an outcome of VNB/APE; strategy remains focused on absolute VNB growth.
Gross-of-GST cost metrics to be reported from end-FY27 onward.
IFRS (Ind AS) reporting to begin April 2027; RBC final form expected soon.
October 2026 trend too early to call (about 10-12 days into the quarter).
capex_capacity: Sum assured market share 11.5% in H1 FY27; sum assured ₹8.81 trillion, up 30.1%.
Opex (ex-GST and stamp duty) down at 8% CAGR over three years, a 22% absolute reduction in FY26 versus FY23.
54% of savings policies issued same day in H1 FY27 through straight-through processing and automation.
Distribution footprint: 2.41 lakh+ advisors, 52 bank partnerships covering 27,000+ bank branches, 1,600+ non-bank partnerships.
demand_pricing: Credit life APE growth described as broadly in line with protection growth; split of credit life by partner not disclosed.
Non-par mix about 60:40 par to non-par in the latest quarter; non-par repriced continuously to market yields and some benefit passed to customers.
Consultation paper proposes a significant cut in credit life commissions (about 2% cap was discussed); management said it is too early to call volume impact.
Renewal commission allowances are significant under the proposal, which management said gives comfort on distributor alignment.
Annuity growth of about 50% across channels, driven by attractive IRRs on regular-pay annuity and guaranteed products.
Persistency: 13th month 84.5%; 25th month 76.2%, down from 77.0% in June; management said the pattern is expected as the cohort rolls forward.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the VNB margin movement is mix versus cost or yield curve, and what drove the GST-inclusive cost ratio rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin expansion is mainly product mix toward protection. The ex-GST cost ratio is highlighted because of the input tax credit challenge from September 2025; gross-of-GST figures will be shown going forward.

qa_highlights.question: What are distributors' initial views on the consultation paper and could it cause near-term volume impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Too early to call; feedback is due to IRDAI by end-October. Management pointed to higher renewal commission allowances as supportive of distributor alignment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the bancassurance slowdown driver and the ICICI Bank share?
qa_highlights.answer: Banca grew about 5% in H1. ICICI Bank is about half of banca and steady at ₹100-120 crore per month, focused on ULIP and protection; growth is coming from other partners.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for H2 retail protection and agency growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail protection growth expected to taper from 40-50% to more moderate levels in H2. Agency is improving with Q2 at 4.1%, but no numeric growth target was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 retail APE growth be guided, and what is the non-par versus par split?
qa_highlights.answer: No guidance given; non-par about 40% and par about 60% in the latest quarter. Credit life is roughly a third of protection, with protection about 23-24% of total APE.

qa_highlights.question: Are operating and investment variances available for H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Not broken out; the total of variances is positive and economic variance is close to zero.

risks_watch: IRDAI distribution consultation paper: commission caps, credit life bundling, and a possible 2% credit life commission cap could hit volumes and partner economics.
Linked savings softness amid equity market volatility; October trend not yet visible.
Persistency: 25th month at 76.2%, down from 77% in June; cohort roll-forward expected to keep pressure on.
Transition to IFRS (April 2027) and RBC could change reported profitability and capital; final RBC form pending.
Agency growth still low single-digit (3.3% H1); management did not commit to double-digit growth.
Retail protection growth tapering in H2 after four quarters of elevated growth.
summary.management_tone: Confident on VNB, margins and cost discipline, but cautious and non-committal on the consultation paper, guidance and H2 growth. Management repeatedly deferred regulatory impact and gave no numbers on credit life payouts or the H1 variance walk.
key_quotes: Our strategy remains unchanged, delivering sustainable VNB growth while balancing business growth, profitability, and risk and prudence.
Margin is just an outcome. It is VNB divided by APE.
So the consistent work that we've been doing on opex actually is giving us these leverage elements here.
We will seek to deliver sustainable growth, Nischint.

growth.why: No formal guidance was given; management only offered medium-term direction, with retail protection growth (40-50%) expected to taper in H2 FY27 and linked savings slowing, so the outlook is unclear.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: VNB margin rose to 26.0% from 24.7% in FY26 (+130 bps) on protection mix (protection share of APE 23.4% vs 19.3%), but management frames margin as an outcome of mix and gave no margin guidance, and the ex-GST cost ratio fell only 30 bps to 18.3%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Brief does not discuss new branches, plants or distribution capacity additions; footprint cited as 2.41 lakh+ advisors, 52 bank partnerships and 1,600+ non-bank partnerships with no expansion plan given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: New business premium grew 25.0% to ₹118.21 bn and protection APE 39.5%, but retail protection growth of 40-50% is expected to taper in H2 FY27, linked savings slowed to 6.6%, and agency grew only 3.3% in H1.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Opex is down 22% in FY26 vs FY23 and 54% of savings policies are issued straight-through, and no utilisation or capex plan was discussed, so there is no sign of a capex announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No formal guidance was given, and management declined to commit on H2 growth, with retail protection tapering and the October trend too early to call.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The IRDAI consultation paper proposes a significant cut to credit life commissions (about 2% cap discussed), management declined to quantify the volume impact, and 25th-month persistency fell to 76.2% from 77.0% in June.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or model launches were discussed; annuity growth of about 50% is from existing products.

rows.label: IRDAI distribution consultation paper (credit life and commission caps)
rows.why: Feedback due to IRDAI by end-October, and a credit life commission cut of about 2% was discussed, with management saying it is too early to call the volume impact.

rows.label: Annuity growth momentum
rows.why: Annuity grew about 50% across channels on attractive regular-pay annuity IRRs and guaranteed products, supporting savings APE (up 9.3% to ₹37.79 bn).

rows.label: Linked savings and non-linked recovery
rows.why: Linked grew 6.6% and softened in late Q2 amid equity weakness, while non-linked fell 4.5% in H1 but Q2 was near last year's level, so recovery depends on markets.

tone.note: Management was confident on VNB growth (+22.3%), margin (26.0%) and cost discipline (opex down 22% in FY26 vs FY23), but cautious and non-committal on the IRDAI consultation paper, H2 retail protection growth and guidance; analysts pushed on the credit life commission cut impact and the H1 variance
